well i dont need the car in the engine immediately. i was more just testing out the block bench app to understand how it handled modeling. and its a better approach than blender, and something that we can replicate here. so this is how i technically see it:

start with the workspace for it, it looks like this [Image #3] 
ok now we then use our layers component and make the outliner layers. this can be a block, a cylinder, any shape we have already demonstrated to work. place it exact at 0,0 for its size [Image #4] [Image #5], then select face [Image #6] and then select the top face [Image #7] or i can select the [Image #8] edge [Image #9] or the vertex [Image #10] [Image #11] 
we already kinda have vertex uv dragging, ours looks like this [Image #12] but ours has a really poor staging area and camera. the camera is actually a large part of the battle that cant be over looked. 

i think that at a minimum start, would be what i would say is the first slice, before we introduce extruding and create face or edge  or loop cutting 

the basics that it all rides on. but if you compare our uv painter grid to the uv display in blockbench, you can se we have a lot in common even if its not exactly the same yet
